$comment: Project-scoped MCP servers. Both are launched from the checkout, never from the network,
so the version an assistant consults is the version this workspace pins (P4).
angular-cli: the Angular CLI's own MCP server (`ng mcp`), from the catalog-pinned
@angular/cli in node_modules. Run `pnpm install` first or it will not start.
WHY --read-only, WHICH IS NOT THE DEFAULT AND NOT CAUTION FOR ITS OWN SAKE:
the server discovers workspaces by walking down from its working directory, and its
exclusion list is hardcoded to node_modules/dist/out/coverage — it does not read
.gitignore. So from the repo root it finds FIVE angular.json files, and two of them are
inside `ref/primeng`: PrimeTek's own showcase app and the `primeng` library itself.
`ref/` is the quarantined evidence clone. Constitution P2: it is read-only, it is never
modified, and it is reproducible from the SHA in PROVENANCE.md. A `run_target` or
`devserver_start` aimed at one of those two projects would write build output, caches and
a lockfile into the directory whose whole value is that nothing has been written into it.
--read-only removes exactly the three tools that can act — run_target, devserver_start,
devserver_stop — and leaves the rest. onpush_zoneless_migration stays and is safe: it
declares isReadOnly and writes nothing (checked, not assumed).
Residual, stated rather than hidden: list_projects still NAMES those two workspaces. That
is informational and harmless — `ref/primeng` is the MIT 21.1.9 clone this project forked
from, so reading it is allowed; only writing to it is not, and nothing here can now write.
`ref/primeng.dev`, the commercial specimen, has no angular.json and is never discovered.
Builds, tests and dev servers are run from the shell instead. That was already the
practice; this makes it the only option rather than a habit.
Known warning: it cannot resolve the framework version because the catalog: protocol is
not a semver comparator. Documentation lookups still work; only version-targeting is blind.
angulux: this repo's own server, answering from corpus/corpus.json. No model has seen
angulux, so without it an assistant reaches for PrimeNG's <p-button>. See
packages/angulux-mcp/README.md.
